title: Clayton to Oakland: the Nonprofit, the Product, and Five Days in November
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Clayton, and the Machine on the Desk

stops.name: Chicago, the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'). No reachable source names the hospital, so the coordinate is the city center and nothing narrower.
stops.campa: Samuel Harris Altman is born in Chicago on the twenty-second of April, 1985, the eldest of four children of Connie Gibstine, a dermatologist, and Jerry Altman, who works in real estate. The family does not stay. Within a few years they move to Missouri, to the town Jerry came from, and Chicago becomes a line on a form rather than a place he can be said to remember. The hospital is not recorded anywhere that can be reached, and neither is the date of the move.
suggested_refs: Birth records of Cook County, Illinois, April 1985, not consulted for this file

stops.name: Clayton, Missouri, the Macintosh
stops.date_confidence: traditional. Sources place the Macintosh 'around age eight,' which would fall in 1993, but no source dates the gift and 1 January is a placeholder for ordering. The family address is not public; the pin is Clayton city center.
stops.campa: In Clayton, a wooded municipality west of St. Louis, the boy is given an Apple Macintosh at about eight years old and teaches himself to program on it. No source dates the gift; 'around age eight' is as close as the record comes. The exact street is not public, and his mother's practice and his father's office sit within a few miles of it. He is Jewish, Midwestern, the eldest of four, and precocious in the way that gets a child moved up a grade and resented for it.
suggested_refs: The Apple Macintosh of the early 1990s, the first computer in the Altman house

stops.name: John Burroughs School, Ladue: the assembly
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Attendance at John Burroughs School and graduation in 2003 are attested (Wikipedia, 'John Burroughs School'), but the assembly survives only in retrospective recollection: no transcript, no school paper, no date within 2001-2003. The date here orders the segment and asserts nothing. Two earlier lenses gave conflicting coordinates, 38.639/-90.3893 and 38.6431/-90.3629; both are reconciled here to the school's own published pin at 755 South Price Road.
stops.campa: At the private preparatory school on South Price Road, students object to a speaker invited for National Coming Out Day. Altman, sixteen or seventeen, stands up before the assembled school and tells it he is gay. The school is in Ladue, immediately west of Clayton, where the family lives. Everything else about the scene is missing: the month, the speaker's name, what he actually said, what the room did. Every profile written since repeats it; not one has produced a piece of paper. He graduates in 2003.
suggested_refs: John Burroughs School yearbooks and student publications, 2001-2003, not located for this file

stops.name: Stanford, the Main Quad: enrollment
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the month is inferred from the ordinary start of the academic year and is not recorded.
stops.campa: He comes to read computer science and stays two years. In the dormitories and the laboratories he meets Nick Sivo, who becomes his co-founder and, for a time, his boyfriend, and the several others who will go into the first company with him. The degree is never finished; he leaves in 2005 with two years of coursework and a partly written product. He will be back on this quadrangle in 2014, running a course called How to Start a Startup, teaching undergraduates how to leave, and the lectures will be posted free for anyone who wants them.
suggested_refs: The Stanford CS106 sequence and the Gates Computer Science Building, 2003-2005
Stanford CS183B, 'How to Start a Startup,' lecture series, autumn 2014

stops.name: Cambridge, Massachusetts: the Summer Founders Program
stops.date_confidence: the inaugural S05 batch ran in Cambridge in the summer of 2005 (Wikipedia, 'Y Combinator'). The specific premises and the exact start date are not recorded, so the coordinate is a general Central Square marker. An earlier lens claimed concurrent Cambridge and Mountain View programs in 2005; the two-coast arrangement in fact began with the Winter 2006 batch, and that claim is not followed here.
stops.campa: Paul Graham and Jessica Livingston run the first Summer Founders Program out of Cambridge, funding eight companies with a few thousand dollars per founder and dinners once a week. Among them is Radiate, three Stanford dropouts building software that puts your friends on a map of the city you are standing in. It will be renamed Loopt. Altman is nineteen. The arrangement has no name yet, no reputation, and no reason for anybody to believe the batch will produce a single surviving company.
suggested_refs: Y Combinator's Summer Founders Program, inaugural batch, 2005

stops.name: Mountain View, seven years of Loopt
stops.date_confidence: the company operated from Mountain View from roughly 2005 through the 2012 sale; the exact street address is not confirmed and the coordinate is downtown Mountain View. This is the atlas's canonical Mountain View pin, inherited byte-identical. The date orders the segment.
stops.campa: For seven years he runs a location-sharing company that is always slightly too early. Loopt raises more than thirty million dollars, signs distribution with the American mobile carriers, ships on the first iPhone, and never finds the users. Altman is chief executive from nineteen to twenty-six, seven years spent keeping a company alive on the strength of the next meeting. The product is correct in every particular. Almost nobody wants, in those years, to be findable on a map by everyone they know.
suggested_refs: Loopt's carrier agreements with Sprint, Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile, 2006-2010
sources: Y Combinator company blog, 'Loopt (YC S05) Acquired by Green Dot for $43.4M'

stops.name: Pasadena, Green Dot buys Loopt
stops.date_confidence: attested (Y Combinator company blog, 'Loopt (YC S05) Acquired by Green Dot for $43.4M'). One lens dated this only to 'March 2012'; the close is 9 March.
stops.campa: The prepaid-card company Green Dot takes Loopt for forty-three million four hundred thousand dollars in cash, of which nine million eight hundred thousand is set aside to retain the staff. Thirty employees cross over and are put to work building a mobile bank called GoBank. Altman becomes executive vice president for mobile products and strategy and joins the Green Dot board the following March. The first company is finished. It returned its investors roughly what they put in, and no more.
stops.quote: We've been doing cool stuff with deals, offers and loyalty, but we haven't had a way to tie that to payments. Now, instead of being about check-ins, it can be about payments.
stops.quote_source: Y Combinator company blog, 'Loopt (YC S05) Acquired by Green Dot for $43.4M,' March 2012
suggested_refs: GoBank, the mobile bank the Loopt team was retained to build
sources: Y Combinator company blog, 'Loopt (YC S05) Acquired by Green Dot for $43.4M'

stops.name: San Francisco, Hydrazine Capital
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 2012 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'). One lens of the research named the wrong brother, Max rather than Jack; Max Altman runs a separate fund. The office address is not public and the coordinate is general San Francisco.
stops.campa: With his brother Jack he raises a venture fund and calls it Hydrazine Capital, putting a large part of it back into Y Combinator companies. Hydrazine is a rocket propellant that decomposes across a catalyst bed and needs no oxidizer at all. He is twenty-seven and out of an operating job for the first time since he was nineteen. The batch and the money turn out to be the same instrument seen from two ends. A third brother, Max, will later run a fund of his own.
suggested_refs: Hydrazine Capital's positions in Y Combinator portfolio companies, 2012-2019

stops.name: Mountain View, part-time partner at Y Combinator
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the month is not recorded and 1 January orders the segment. The address 335 Pioneer Way is Y Combinator's office from 2009 to 2023.
stops.campa: While Loopt is dying he begins coming to Mountain View one day a week to sit on the other side of the table. The arrangement lasts three years. Graham has him read applications, deliver the ten-minute verdicts, argue at the Tuesday dinners. He is a graduate of the first batch, which inside this institution counts as lineage. The building on Pioneer Way is low and wide, long tables, no reception desk. The firm has been there since 2009 and will stay until 2023.
suggested_refs: Y Combinator's office at 335 Pioneer Way, Mountain View, 2009-2023

stops.name: Mountain View, Graham names his successor
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 2014 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the day is not recorded here.
stops.campa: Paul Graham, who founded the accelerator and ran it for nine years, hands the presidency to a twenty-eight-year-old and steps back from the running of it. What passes with the title is two batches a year, several hundred companies, and the demo days at which a room of investors decides which of them will go on existing. Altman says at once that he intends to fund harder things than software, fission and fusion and biotechnology among them, and he begins doing exactly that inside the first year.
suggested_refs: Paul Graham's announcement of the Y Combinator succession, February 2014

stops.name: Big Sur, the list
stops.date_confidence: the New Yorker profile is dated October 2016; the day is a placeholder. The quotation is verified verbatim through Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman,' the magazine's own page being unreachable from here. The coordinate is the Big Sur village and Pfeiffer area, not the parcel, which is not publicly identified; an earlier lens described it as the Bixby Bridge area, which lies twenty-five kilometres north.
stops.campa: Tad Friend, reporting a profile for The New Yorker, asks the president of Y Combinator what he would do if it all came apart, and gets an inventory in reply. Guns, gold, potassium iodide, antibiotics, batteries, water, gas masks from the Israeli army, and a stretch of coast south of Carmel he can reach by air. Seven years later he says the story was a caricature and that no bunker would help anybody if artificial general intelligence went wrong. The list itself he has never withdrawn.
stops.quote: I have guns, gold, potassium iodide, antibiotics, batteries, water, gas masks from the Israeli Defense Force, and a big patch of land in Big Sur I can fly to.
stops.quote_source: Sam Altman, quoted in Tad Friend, 'Sam Altman's Manifest Destiny,' The New Yorker, October 2016
suggested_refs: Tad Friend, 'Sam Altman's Manifest Destiny,' The New Yorker, October 2016
sources: Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman', quoting the New Yorker profile

stops.name: Mountain View, the Thiel partnership severed
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 2017 in peter_thiel.journey.json. That file does not name Altman in the decision and no source reachable here places him in the room; his involvement is inferred from the presidency he held throughout. Canonical Mountain View pin inherited byte-identical.
stops.campa: Y Combinator ends its part-time-partner arrangement with Peter Thiel, a year after Thiel's endorsement of Donald Trump split the firms and the founders around him. Thiel had been a part-time partner of the firm and is a fixture of the funding network the accelerator sits inside. Altman is president throughout the affair; the institution doing the severing is his to run. No source reachable from here places him in the decision, quotes him on it, or records what was said in the room, and neither the firm nor Thiel has published an account of it.
suggested_refs: Y Combinator's statement on the end of Peter Thiel's part-time partnership, November 2017

stops.name: Mountain View, Ralston succeeds him
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 2019 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the day is not recorded.
stops.campa: After five years he leaves the presidency to Geoff Ralston and goes full time to the laboratory he has been chairing on the side. Under him the accelerator funded Airbnb, Stripe, Coinbase, Instacart, and several thousand companies that did not become nouns. He is thirty-three, and he has been inside Y Combinator, first as a founder and then as partner and president, for fourteen years. He keeps no operating role in the industry's clearing house after this date.
suggested_refs: Y Combinator's announcement of Geoff Ralston's presidency, March 2019

stops.name: Pioneer Building, San Francisco: Introducing OpenAI
stops.date_confidence: OpenAI Inc. was formed 8 December 2015 and the public announcement was published 11 December 2015 (Wikipedia, 'OpenAI'). The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from elon_musk.journey.json, which places the founding at the Pioneer Building; the geography lens instead reports that the lab worked out of Greg Brockman's living room until September 2016. The contradiction is recorded here and not resolved.
stops.campa: Eleven people announce a nonprofit artificial-intelligence laboratory with a billion dollars pledged against it and a charter saying the results will be given away. The stated reason for existing is that somebody will build this and it had better not be only a company. Elon Musk and Altman are co-chairs. The rest of the founding list is Ilya Sutskever, Greg Brockman, Andrej Karpathy, John Schulman, Wojciech Zaremba, Durk Kingma, Trevor Blackwell, Vicki Cheung and Pamela Vagata. The corporation is three days old on the day of the announcement.
suggested_refs: OpenAI, 'Introducing OpenAI,' 11 December 2015
elon_musk.journey.json, for the Pioneer Building pin

stops.name: Pioneer Building, the compute bill
stops.date_confidence: the move into the Pioneer Building is dated September 2016 (Wikipedia, 'OpenAI'); the funding bridge is dated 2017 in reid_hoffman.journey.json with no month, so 1 January is a placeholder for ordering only.
stops.campa: The lab takes a converted chocolate factory at 3180 Eighteenth Street in the Mission, and stays in it into the early 2020s. The pledged billion is a pledge and not a balance, and the training runs cost money for every hour they run. Reid Hoffman, among the earliest funders, covers a compute bill when the money is short. He will later sit on the board that fires Altman and on the board that takes him back. The sources reachable here give the year of the bridge and not the month.
suggested_refs: The Pioneer Building, 3180 18th Street, San Francisco, OpenAI headquarters 2016 to the early 2020s

stops.name: Waterloo, Ontario: the honorary doctorate
stops.date_confidence: the University of Waterloo's own convocation-highlights page confirms an Honorary Doctor of Engineering in June 2017. It gives no day, no time and no hall, and it does not say he addressed the graduates, naming a different honorand for that. Earlier claims of 17 June, 2:30 p.m., the Physical Activities Complex, and a convocation address are struck. The afterlife lens gave 43.4738; the campus pin used here is 43.4723.
stops.campa: A Canadian engineering faculty gives the college dropout an honorary doctorate in engineering, twelve years after he left Stanford without one and fourteen after he enrolled. The university's own notice records that during the visit he met student entrepreneurs and ran a Startup School session on the campus. It does not record him speaking at the ceremony; that fell, the same page says, to the chemist Chunli Bai. The day of the convocation, the hall, the hour, and anything he might have said from a podium are not preserved on any page that can be reached.
suggested_refs: University of Waterloo, 'June 2017 convocation highlights,' uwaterloo.ca

stops.name: Redmond, Washington: the billion
stops.date_confidence: the investment is attested to 2019 without a month in the sources reachable here; 1 January is a placeholder for ordering within the year.
stops.campa: Microsoft puts a billion dollars into OpenAI and becomes its principal cloud partner and, in practice, its only one. Much of the money is credit against Azure rather than cash, which means the investment and the compute are the same thing. From here the laboratory's capacity to run an experiment at all is a line item in another corporation's data centres, subject to another corporation's capital plans. No month for the investment is established in any source reachable here.
suggested_refs: The Microsoft-OpenAI partnership agreement of 2019 and its Azure exclusivity terms
sources: Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'

stops.name: San Francisco, the capped profit and the chief executive's chair
stops.date_confidence: the restructuring and Altman's assumption of the chief executive's title are attested to 2019 without a month in the sources reachable here. The placeholder orders the year after the March departure from Y Combinator. The pin is general San Francisco.
stops.campa: OpenAI builds a for-profit subsidiary underneath the nonprofit: investor returns capped at a fixed multiple, everything above the cap flowing back to the charity, and the nonprofit board holding control over the whole of it. Altman leaves Y Combinator that spring and takes the chief executive's title here. He holds no equity in the thing, a fact he offers as proof of disinterest and which others read as leverage of a different kind. The structure is a lawyer's answer to an engineer's problem. The nonprofit board keeps the power to remove him.
suggested_refs: OpenAI LP's capped-profit charter and the nonprofit board's control provisions, 2019

stops.name: Pioneer Building, ChatGPT
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'ChatGPT'), and confirmed by Altman's own account in 'Reflections.'
stops.campa: A research preview goes up with no marketing behind it, a text box on a white page and a warning that the system may be wrong about things. Inside the building the expectation is a modest week and a few tens of thousands of curious users. It reaches a hundred million faster than anything in the consumer record. The working name had been Chat with GPT-3.5. Nothing about the underlying model is new that November; the model has existed inside the company for months and been available to developers. What is new is that it will talk to anybody who types.
stops.quote: We ended up mercifully calling it ChatGPT instead, and launched it on November 30th of 2022.
suggested_refs: John Searle's Chinese Room argument (1980), against which the product is routinely read
john_searle.journey.json

stops.name: Pioneer Building, GPT-4
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'OpenAI').
stops.campa: GPT-4 ships to the interface and to paying subscribers on the same day. Eleven days earlier Reid Hoffman resigned from the OpenAI board, citing the conflict of running Inflection AI while sitting on a competitor's board; ten days after the release he publishes a book written in conversation with this model. Twenty-two days before it, a letter signed by thousands had asked the laboratories to pause anything more powerful than this exact release for six months. Nothing pauses.
suggested_refs: The Future of Life Institute open letter of 22 March 2023, naming GPT-4 as its threshold
yoshua_bengio.journey.json
ray_kurzweil.journey.json

stops.name: Dirksen Senate Office Building, Washington: the testimony
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the specific hearing room within the building is not independently confirmed here. A second appearance, before the Senate Commerce Committee on 8 May 2025, is attested only through a committee testimony PDF that could not be fetched, and its building could not be established at all, so it is given no stop.
stops.campa: Before the Senate Judiciary subcommittee on privacy, technology and the law, he asks to be regulated. He proposes licensing for models above a capability threshold, safety testing before deployment, an international body on the model of the atomic energy agency. Senators who spent two decades failing to regulate social media are presented with a chief executive volunteering for the leash, and several say aloud that the experience is new to them. No statute has followed from the hearing.
suggested_refs: U.S. Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology and the Law, hearing of 16 May 2023, judiciary.senate.gov

stops.name: San Francisco, the one-sentence statement
stops.date_confidence: the statement's date and Altman's signature are attested (Wikipedia, 'Statement on AI risk of extinction'). One lens dated it only to '2023.' No source places him anywhere in particular when he signed, so the pin is his own city and asserts nothing about his whereabouts.
stops.campa: The Center for AI Safety publishes a single sentence and collects signatures under it. Altman signs. So does Geoffrey Hinton, who had left Google that month precisely in order to be free to say such things, and so do Yoshua Bengio and Demis Hassabis. Two weeks after asking Congress to license his industry, the man selling the product puts his name to a document that sets it beside pandemics and nuclear war, and goes on shipping. How a man signs that sentence in the morning and ships the product in the afternoon is not a question the record answers.
stops.quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.
stops.quote_source: Center for AI Safety, statement on AI risk, 30 May 2023
suggested_refs: geoffrey_hinton.journey.json, for the same signature gathered in Toronto
sources: Wikipedia, 'Statement on AI risk of extinction'

stops.name: 10 Downing Street, London
stops.date_confidence: the meeting with Rishi Sunak is attested to May 2023 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the day is not recorded and the venue is inferred from the office Sunak held rather than from a record of the meeting place.
stops.campa: The tour begins in Europe and runs through more than twenty countries across May and June, palace to palace, Paris and Madrid and Berlin and Jerusalem among the stops. In London he meets the British prime minister and discusses a national safety institute. In the same week he tells an audience that his company might have to leave Europe if the draft AI Act is passed as written, and inside a few days he retracts it. The venue here is inferred from the office Sunak held, not from any record of where the two men sat.
suggested_refs: The UK AI Safety Summit of November 2023, prepared in part through these May meetings

stops.name: Berlaymont, Brussels
stops.date_confidence: the meeting with Ursula von der Leyen is attested to May 2023 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the venue is inferred from the Commission President's seat and the day is not recorded.
stops.campa: The European Commission is finishing the world's first comprehensive statute on artificial intelligence, and the man whose product occasioned much of its final drafting comes to see its president. The Act will grade systems by risk and impose obligations on general-purpose models by name. He tells the Europeans he supports regulation. He has already told a London room that his company might have to withdraw from the continent. Both sentences are on the record inside eight days.
suggested_refs: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act, general-purpose model provisions, drafted 2023

stops.name: New Delhi, 7 Lok Kalyan Marg
stops.date_confidence: the meeting with Narendra Modi is attested to June 2023 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the venue is inferred from the prime minister's residence and the day is not recorded.
stops.campa: In India he meets the prime minister and speaks to rooms for which the question is not extinction but whether a country of a billion four hundred million people will be a market for this technology or a builder of it. Asked in public whether a small Indian team could build something competitive from scratch on a modest budget, he says it would be hopeless for them to try, and adds that they should try anyway. He walks the first half back afterward. In India it is the first half that gets remembered, and it is quoted against him for years.
suggested_refs: Altman's public session in New Delhi, June 2023, and the 'hopeless' exchange

stops.name: Seoul, the Yongsan presidential office
stops.date_confidence: the meeting with Yoon Suk-yeol is attested to June 2023 (Wikipedia, 'Sam Altman'); the day is not recorded. The coordinate is corrected to the Yongsan compound at 22 Itaewon-ro; an earlier lens gave 37.5326/126.9909, about 1.3 km southeast of it. Other capitals on the same tour, Paris, Madrid, Berlin, Jerusalem, are attested but given no stop of their own here; see the report.
stops.campa: The last leg reaches the president of South Korea in the former defence ministry compound at Yongsan, a building the administration had moved into the previous year, and the conversation turns to Korean semiconductors and Korean start-ups. Samsung and SK Hynix between them make most of the world's high-bandwidth memory, and every model he intends to train for the rest of the decade will run on their output. Six weeks of meetings with heads of government about safety and licensing end here, at 22 Itaewon-ro, talking about chips.
suggested_refs: Korean high-bandwidth memory production at Samsung and SK Hynix, the physical constraint on model training

stops.name: Las Vegas, the video call
stops.date_confidence: attested (Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'): Altman was in Las Vegas for the Grand Prix and was notified by video call five to ten minutes before the public announcement. The coordinate is the city, no named building being recorded. The quotation is relayed through Wikipedia's account of the removal; the original post on X could not be fetched here.
stops.campa: He is in Nevada for the Formula One street race, the weekend the circuit runs down the Strip, when a Google Meet invitation arrives. Ilya Sutskever, his own co-founder, is on the call and tells him the board has removed him as chief executive. The call takes a few minutes. Between five and ten minutes after it ends the board's blog post goes up, and the head of the most watched company in the world learns the remainder of it the same way the rest of the world does. That afternoon he posts a single sentence, in lower case.
stops.quote: i loved my time at openai. it was transformative for me personally, and hopefully the world a little bit.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Sam Altman, post on X, 17 November 2023, relayed through Wikipedia's account of the removal
suggested_refs: The Las Vegas Grand Prix, 16-18 November 2023
sources: Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'

stops.name: Pioneer Building, the board's sentence
stops.date_confidence: attested. The board's wording is quoted through Wikipedia's account, openai.com returning 403 to direct fetch and washingtonpost.com being unreachable here. One lens attributed the phrase to the Washington Post rather than to the board statement the Post was reporting; corrected. One lens also placed OpenAI headquarters at 37.7699/-122.4009 for this date, which is Potrero, not the Mission; the Pioneer Building pin is used.
stops.campa: Four directors, Helen Toner, Adam D'Angelo, Tasha McCauley and Ilya Sutskever, publish the sentence that will be read ten thousand times in the following week and explained by none of them. The full clause is that he was not consistently candid in his communications with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities. Greg Brockman is removed as chairman and resigns within hours. Mira Murati is named interim chief executive the same day. The board does not say what he was not candid about. It has still not said.
stops.quote: not consistently candid in his communications with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities
stops.quote_source: OpenAI board statement, 'OpenAI announces leadership transition,' 17 November 2023, as reported by the Washington Post
suggested_refs: OpenAI, 'OpenAI announces leadership transition,' 17 November 2023, openai.com
sources: Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'

stops.name: San Francisco, seven hundred and forty-five names
stops.date_confidence: the letter circulated on 20 November 2023 and signatures grew that day from about five hundred to 745 of roughly 770 employees (Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'). One lens dated it 21 November, off by one day, and gave the count as 'more than 500'; corrected.
stops.campa: Satya Nadella announces that Altman and Brockman will lead a new advanced research group inside Microsoft, and the OpenAI board appoints Emmett Shear, formerly of Twitch, as its second interim chief executive in three days. Then the staff answer. A letter circulates threatening mass resignation unless the board goes, and by evening seven hundred and forty-five of about seven hundred and seventy employees have signed it. Ilya Sutskever, who made the call to Las Vegas, signs it too.
suggested_refs: The OpenAI employee open letter of 20 November 2023
sources: Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'

stops.name: San Francisco, the return
stops.date_confidence: the agreement in principle was reached late on 21 November Pacific time and the reinstatement is dated 22 November 2023 (Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'). One lens of the research dated the return to the 21st and another to the 22nd; the discrepancy is recorded rather than smoothed.
stops.campa: The agreement is reached late on the night of the twenty-first, Pacific time, and Altman and Brockman come back on the twenty-second. An interim board of three is seated, Bret Taylor as chairman with Adam D'Angelo and Lawrence Summers, and Altman does not take a seat on it. Of the four directors who removed him, one remains. The nonprofit control structure built in 2019 to restrain a chief executive was tested exactly once and did not hold for five days. No two accounts published since by the people in the room agree with each other.
suggested_refs: The reconstituted OpenAI interim board of 22 November 2023
sources: Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'

stops.name: San Francisco, the photograph
stops.date_confidence: TIME's Chief Executive of the Year issue is dated 6 December 2023; the cover photograph by Joe Pugliese was made in San Francisco on 8 November 2023, nine days before the removal.
stops.campa: TIME's issue of the sixth of December names him chief executive of the year. The profile calls him a prophet of a technological revolution and quotes unnamed colleagues calling him slippery in the pursuit of consolidating power. The cover has been decided before the firing, and the issue runs as planned. Joe Pugliese makes the photograph in San Francisco on the eighth of November, nine days before the board's call, in a grey sweater and brightly coloured Adidas.
stops.quote: the public face and leading prophet of a technological revolution
stops.quote_source: TIME, 'CEO of the Year 2023: Sam Altman,' time.com/6342827
suggested_refs: Joe Pugliese's cover portrait for TIME, made 8 November 2023
sources: TIME, 'CEO of the Year 2023: Sam Altman,' time.com/6342827

stops.name: San Francisco, WilmerHale
stops.date_confidence: attested to 8 March 2024 (Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'). Only a summary of the review was published; the full report was not.
stops.campa: The outside firm hired to review the November events reports that the prior board had acted within its discretion and that Altman's conduct did not mandate removal. He returns to the board four months after being put off it. Sue Desmond-Hellmann, Nicole Seligman and Fidji Simo join at the same time. The review's full text is not published; a summary of it is. Whatever the four directors believed they knew in November is now the property of a law firm's file room, and neither the company nor the directors have added anything to the record since.
suggested_refs: OpenAI's published summary of the WilmerHale review, March 2024
sources: Wikipedia, 'Removal of Sam Altman from OpenAI'

stops.name: Everett, Washington: Helion
stops.date_confidence: the $500 million Series E is attested to November 2021 (Wikipedia, 'Helion Energy'); the day is not recorded. Larger cumulative personal figures reported elsewhere, of roughly $375 million and above, were not independently verified here.
stops.campa: North of Seattle, in a shed on a business park, a company builds a pulsed magneto-inertial fusion machine that fires plasma rings into each other and draws electricity straight back out of the collapsing field, skipping the steam turbine entirely.
